summary: Specializing in religious studies and sinology, Cuma Ozkan earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, and served as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

A scholar in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Cynthea J. Bogel completed doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield. She held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2004–2009).
Cynthia Col studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman, working in the fields of sinology and religious studies.
Cynthia M. Beall studied at Pennsylvania State University (~1970–1976) and joined Case Western Reserve University in 1976, working in Tibetology and other fields.

Cynthia Talbot is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1978–1988). She served on the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1995 to 2021, where she is professor emeritus.

Cyril Henry Philips studied history at the University of Liverpool (1931–1934) and SOAS (~1936–1940). An Indology and history scholar, he succeeded Ralph Lilley Turner as Director of SOAS in 1957 and served as vice-chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, having also studied under Turrell V. Wylie, Dezhung Rinpoche, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she also held a position as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau studied at the University of Hong Kong under Xu Dishan and at the University of Glasgow. A sinologist and philosopher, he held posts at SOAS, the University of London, UCL, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati studied Indology under V. Raghavan and served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College from circa 1970 to 2005.
D. L. Narasimhachar studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1927–1932) and held a post at the University of Mysore (~1932–1962), working in the fields of Indology and linguistics.
D. N. Shukla earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. An Indologist, he held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

D. Neil Schmid works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.
D. R. Nagaraj, an Indologist, studied at Bangalore University (~1974–1979) and later held a post there from circa 1979 to 1998.
D. S. Subbaramaiya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.
D. Srinivasachar worked in Indology, serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 1931–1933).

Dagfinn Føllesdal studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine. In philosophy and linguistics, he taught at Harvard, became Professor Emeritus at the University of Oslo, and was Clarence Irving Lewis Professor of Philosophy Emeritus at Stanford University (1968–2011).
